question.problem: Jack wants to buy a single issue of a particular comic series with $55$ issues. Unfortunately, the comic store does not have the first $7$ issues in stock. If Jack buys a comic at random from the available issues, what is the standard deviation of the issue numbers he could select? Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the number of the issue Jack selects. From the problem statement, we know that $X∼U\{8,9,…,55\},$ and we wish to compute $\text{SD}[X].$

In general, if $X∼U\{a,a+1,…,b\},$ then the variance of $X$ is

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\frac{|S{|}^{2}-1}{12}
$$

where $S=\{a,a+1,…,b\}.$

Now, we know that

$$
\begin{aligned}|S| & =b-a+1 \\  & =55-8+1 \\  & =48.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for our random variable $X∼U\{8,9,…,55\},$ we have the following variance:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\frac{{48}^{2}-1}{12}=\frac{2303}{12}
$$

Finally,

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\frac{2303}{12}}≈13.85.
$$
